questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Tangent Under a Modified Domain
questions.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=0$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $0$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=0.$

To generate more solutions, we add integer multiples of $\pi .$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=\pi +{x}_{1}=\pi +0=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x=0,\pi .$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=0\cdot \pi =0.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Points of Intersection of a Horizontal Line and a Tangent Curve
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14040762/assets/f00d8bd6cbd1f113df7f023e161e4d79e2f4a81157d1ac9a8ab65e70b4959221.png)

The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.$  Find the $x$-coordinate of the point $B.$
questions.worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}
$$

 Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

This value lies inside $-\pi \le x<\pi $ hence, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{6}.$ This is the $x$ coordinate of $A.$

To get another solution, we add $\pi $ to the principal value. Thus,

$$
{x}_{2}=\pi +x=\pi -\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{5\pi }{6}.
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $B$ is $\frac{5\pi }{6}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Tangent with Non-Special Angles
questions.problem: Solve the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=8$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(8)=82.874\,983{…}^{∘}≈{82.87}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${82.87}^{∘}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={82.87}^{∘}.$

To generate more solutions, we add integer multiples of ${180}^{∘}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}={180}^{∘}+{82.87}^{∘}={262.87}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are

$$
x={83}^{∘},{263}^{∘}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

$$

$$

Since ${0}^{∘}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={0}^{∘}.$
